title: How a hash table grows
sub: Keys land in buckets by hash. When the table gets crowded it doubles and re-hashes everything, which is what keeps lookups fast.
aria: A hash table drawn as rows of buckets, each holding a chain of colored key chips
breakLabel: 💥 Break it: never resize the table
breakOff: Normal run: the table doubles whenever items ÷ buckets passes the threshold.
breakOn: Resizing is switched off. The bucket count never changes, so chains keep growing and every insert has to walk a longer list.
learn: Each key goes to bucket hash(key) mod buckets. Two keys in one bucket is a collision, and they form a chain.
A resize is expensive (every key moves), but it happens rarely and halves the load factor. Total work stays roughly linear.
Notice keys jump to different buckets after a resize, because the modulus changed. Same hash, new home.
Turn on Break it: chains grow linearly, so inserts and lookups drift from O(1) toward O(n).
